reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound, linking boron-induced grain boundary precipitates to constrained defect mobility and improved high-temperature strength, though the specific alloy (NbTaHfTiZrV0.5) and the exact role of V are less commonly studied, introducing minor uncertainty.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with well-defined conditions, measurements, and a decisive falsification criterion, though integrating in-situ TEM/EBSD with quantitative analysis at these temperatures is technically challenging.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful, offering a specific, testable mechanism (boride pinning of grain boundaries) for a well-known problem (softening in RHEAs) that would guide alloy design if validated.
